# Question and summary

This poster discuss the complexity of finding the ground state of a $k$-local Hamiltonian.

Given $L \in \mathbf{QMA}$,
we conclude that there exists a quantum circuit $U_1,\cdots,U_T$ and a random variable $V(\ket{x},\ket{\xi}) \in\{0,1\}$ such that
$$
\begin{align*}
&x\in L
\Longleftrightarrow
\exists |\xi\rangle \text{ such that } \Pr[V(|x\rangle,|\xi\rangle)=1]\ge 1-\varepsilon,\\
&\Pr[V(\ket{x},\ket{\xi})=1]=\left\|
\bigl(|1\rangle\langle 1|_1\otimes I\bigr)U_T\cdots U_1\bigl(|x\rangle \otimes |\xi\rangle )
\right\|^2,
\end{align*}
$$
where $|x| = n$ and $|\xi| = \mathrm{poly}(n)$ is the qubit number of the certificate.

Use these existed $U_1,\cdots,U_T$, we now find $H(x)$ such that $x\in L \Rightarrow \lambda_{\min}(H(x))\le a$ and $x\notin L \Rightarrow \lambda_{\min}(H(x))\ge b$ for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$.
